pr_title: feat: support `mask` option in screenshot methods

issue_context.title: Hide/remove Elements from Screenshots
issue_context.body:
### Discussed in https://github.com/microsoft/playwright/discussions/5068
Originally posted by **rollin-cogers** January 20, 2021 Hey everyone! I've been very excited to use this tool for testing, as I've previously been using protractor for all my testing. In the past I've used modules like webdriver-image-comparison that allow for options like [hiding and removing elements](https://github.com/wswebcreation/webdriver-image-comparison/blob/master/docs/OPTIONS.md#hideelements-5) from a screenshot by adding `visibility: hidden` or `display: none` to the styling for the passed elements. Is this a feature that we might see in the future with playwright? Would anyone else benefit from the ability to exclude elements from screenshots? I would love to see something like this: ```javascript page.screenshot({fullpage: true, hideElements: ['div.dynamic_content', 'div#profilePicture']}) ```
comments:
Please consider allowing Playwright Users to define how element will be hidden. 

We are currently adding, and removing a class that makes text and background colors black so that the element is still on screenshot, just it's dynamic content does not affect screenshot tests. Some cases would need display:none.
@Evilweed you know your use case better than anyone, but rather than `display: none`, but Playwright should rather use `visibility: hidden` to hide elements without effecting the layout of the page.

Could you elaborate in what it does? Blackout seems to make the area of the element black instead of whatever color it has. This can be a problem if e.g. a fullscreen popup comes with transparent background. Will render the whole page black. Hehe.

But if it does visibility: hidden on them it should not really affect anything :) Other than that, I think it is a perfect implementation! :)

Perfect!
The only objection is about the term `blackout`. Let's change for something more generic e.g. `hide`, or `hideElements`

nice cool work @aslushnikov, I wanted to use that mask feature but it is not ready yet on 1.19.2, what is the easiest way to point out the main branch in order to use it on npm, since I currently have `"@playwright/test": "1.19.2"`
@ph4un00b Playwright 1.20 is coming out in a few days. Meanwhile, you can install Playwright from tip-of-tree using `npm i @playwright/test@next`
@ph4un00b yep, totally expected. In this case, it seems like using request interception to feed in some different image would work better for you!

Can not find any docs for this feature is it still present or was deprecated? 

_upd: found in source code this feature called as "mask", but still wondering about doc_

In our case, dynamic content results in elements with all sorts of different height values.  Because of this, there are still differences even when using the mask feature.  Would be great if there was an option to set the color used for the mask.  

In my case I'd set it to the pages background color.
For posterity, the `mask` option is documented [here](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot)

Mask option does not work for cases If some elements appeared on the page because of rendering through SSR, It's hard to mock API and it would be really nice to have either option to mock SSR or hide elements from the page, for example global messages toast

I ran into an issue with the mask feature and a `position: fixed` element. The mask is layered over the element I am trying to take a screenshot of. Similar to the issue @ph4un00b ran into. Is there a way to hide the masked element's visibility completely? Looking for a way to set `visibility: none;` on that element

Some masks cause an overlay due to the masked item having `position: absolute`. This causes an issue where I am not able to screenshot the elements that are beneath the masked element's layer when attempting to screenshot a full page.
@Albert-Valdes I ended up just using `page.evaluate()` to hide my elements manually, though I will keep the mask options in mind for future tasks.

For those coming here, you can inject a css file when running the tests...
https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-screenshot

To configure it globally:
https://playwright.dev/docs/test-configuration#expect-options

In short: pass options with { stylePath: "e2e.css" }.
Hope it help

This issue aught to be re-opened as the `mask` property does NOT solve all use-cases, as others mentions here that the mask is covering OVER the masked area which is in MANY cases not the desired outcome at all, which is to _HIDE_ page elements and _NOT_ mask them, because any element which is rendered at a masked X & Y position will also be masked, and I find this absurd for UI testing which usually has complex common scenarios with tooltips/popups and transformed elements which can appear.. anywhere over the masked area.

At the minimum, if we must resort to manual-labor by hard-coding styles to hide elements, at least align the options of [`toHaveScreenshot`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-pageassertions#methods) with [`screenshot`](https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-page#page-screenshot) to allow `style` property (as a string-injected styles)

I really plead for this issue to be re-opened as this is a **very** basic and important thing playwright is expected to support out-of-the-box for UI screenshot tests, so please please give it a thought.

I have resorted to manual style-injections which runs after every `goto()` command:
